references.text: The same chapter describes that the unclean must cleanse themselves on the third and seventh days to become clean; otherwise, they remain unclean.
Describes the procedure of using hyssop to sprinkle water for cleansing on unclean persons and objects.
A similar cleansing ritual where the person must wash their clothes, bathe in water, and become clean.
Prescribes washing clothes and bathing in water as part of the cleansing process from uncleanness.
Washing clothes and uncleanness lasting until evening is a recurring pattern in the laws of purity.
Describes washing clothes and bathing as necessary to become clean by evening.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to the sprinkling of the unclean with the ashes of a heifer as an image of the cleansing power of Christ's blood.
Speaks of being sprinkled clean from a guilty conscience and washed with pure water, alluding to Old Testament cleansing rituals.
